exposure: delivery modality (vaginal delivery vs. cesarean section)
outcome: umbilical cord gas analysis (oxygen, lactate, carbon dioxide)
cohort: healthy newborns with gestational age ≥37 weeks
finding: Fetal oxygenation levels increase progressively from 37 to 41 weeks gestation, suggesting a progressive shift from anaerobic to aerobic metabolism in utero.
mod_finding: In neonates born by vaginal delivery, the increased oxygen availability is associated with a modest increase in oxygen extraction, while in neonates born by cesarean section, it is associated with reduced lactate production.
